- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) and forecast is low, increase forecast by 15–30% to capture bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33) and forecast is high, reduce forecast by 20–40% to avoid overreaction.  
- After a sharp spike in sentiment or price, model tends to overshoot — cap forecast at 1.5x the prior 7-day average to prevent runaway growth.  
- If sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.33) and forecast is high, apply a 10–20% downward correction to avoid false optimism.  
- If history shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of price decline), model often undercorrects — add 5–10% to forecast to anticipate reversal.  
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, if sentiment is volatile or mixed, reduce forecast by 10–15% to account for uncertainty and lag.
